changes: date.paksa normalised to 'kṛṣṇa (badi)'; date.tithi given as '30 (amāvāsyā)'. 'pratipadcchuddhā' is noted as probably meaning the śukla pratipad that follows, or the tithi being 'pure'
notes expanded: no scribe or place is named in the quoted colophon; the catalogue's ŚS reading is unsupported; 'sakalaśāstraprvīṇa' corrected to pravīṇa
Persons, relation (Rāghava son_of Pṛthvīdhara), year and ce_approx 1691 (VS) confirmed

notes: The colophon gives only 'saṃvat 1748' with no era named. In a Devanagari north-Indian manuscript, 'saṃvat' normally means Vikrama, so I read it as VS 1748 ≈ 1691 CE. The catalogue reads ŚS 1748 (≈1826 CE), but nothing in the quoted colophon supports that. The catalogue gives Kāśī as the place of copying, but the quoted colophon names no place; it may come from elsewhere in the manuscript, so it is left empty here. No scribe, commissioner or owner is named. The only persons are the commentator Rāghavabhaṭṭa (author of the Śākuntala commentary, the Arthadyotanikā) and his father Pṛthvīdhara. 'pratipadcchuddhā' after 'badi 30' is unclear. It may mean that the following śukla pratipad was 'pure' (śuddhā), or that the amāvāsyā ran into the pratipad. The cataloguer's 'prvīṇa' is a typo for pravīṇa.
